description: Residential solar installer with a customer monitoring app (Brightline Home) and an installer/partner API. 36 articles across FAQ, Procedure, and News record types.

articles.title: Why is my monthly bill higher than the estimate in my proposal?
articles.summary: Common reasons a Brightline invoice exceeds the original production estimate, and how to check each one.
articles.question: My proposal said I'd pay about $118/month. My last two invoices were $164 and $171. Why?
articles.answer:
Short answer

Your invoice has two parts: the fixed financing payment (which never changes) and the utility true-up for any power you drew from the grid. The second part is what moves.

Check these first

  1. Production vs. estimate. Open Brightline Home → Reports → Monthly Production and compare to the proposal. Anything below 85% of estimate for two months in a row should be reported as low production.
  2. Usage increase. A new EV charger, heat pump, or pool pump can add 300–600 kWh/month.
  3. Utility rate change. Most utilities adjusted time-of-use rates in the last 12 months. Your true-up is billed at the utility's current rate, not the rate in the proposal.
  4. Shading or soiling. See cleaning your panels.
Line itemChanges month to month?Where to check
Financing paymentNoLoan agreement
Utility true-upYesUtility bill, page 2
Monitoring subscriptionOnly at renewalAccount → Plan

Note: Brightline does not bill you for grid power. That charge comes from your utility; we show it in the app for convenience.

articles.title: When are invoices issued and when is payment due?
articles.summary: Invoice timing, due dates, and what happens if a payment is late.
articles.question: What day of the month does Brightline invoice me, and how long do I have to pay?
articles.answer:
Invoices are generated on the 1st of each month and are due on the 15th. You'll receive an email the morning the invoice is ready, and it appears under Billing → Invoices in Brightline Home.

  • Autopay customers are charged on the 10th.
  • A late fee of $15 applies after the 20th.
  • Two consecutive missed payments pause monitoring alerts (production continues uninterrupted).

To change your billing date, see Change your billing date.

articles.title: What payment methods does Brightline accept?
articles.summary: Accepted payment methods and any associated fees.
articles.question: Can I pay by credit card?
articles.answer:
Yes. Accepted methods:

  • ACH bank transfer — no fee, recommended
  • Debit card — no fee
  • Credit card (Visa, Mastercard, Amex) — 2.9% processing fee
  • Check — mail to the address on your invoice; allow 7 business days

We do not accept cash, cryptocurrency, or third-party payment apps. To set up autopay, follow Set up autopay.

articles.title: Can I pay off my solar loan early?
articles.summary: Early payoff rules, how to request a payoff quote, and tax credit timing.
articles.question: I received my federal tax credit. Can I apply it to the loan?
articles.answer:
Yes, and this is the most common use of the credit. All Brightline financing is prepayment-penalty free.

To make a one-time principal payment

  1. Go to Billing → Financing → Make a principal payment.
  2. Enter the amount. Payments under $500 are applied at the next statement; larger payments are applied within 2 business days.
  3. Your monthly payment is re-amortized automatically — it goes down, the term stays the same.
If you'd rather keep the payment the same and shorten the term, contact Financing Support and ask for a term-reduction instead of re-amortization. This must be requested before the payment is applied.

For a full payoff quote, use Billing → Financing → Request payoff quote. Quotes are valid for 10 days.

articles.title: Is the federal solar tax credit still available?
articles.summary: Current status of the residential clean energy credit and what Brightline provides for your tax filing.
articles.question: Do I still qualify for the 30% tax credit?
articles.answer:
Tax law changes frequently and Brightline is not a tax advisor. What we can tell you:

  • The credit is claimed on your federal return for the tax year the system was placed in service (the date your utility granted permission to operate, not the install date).
  • Brightline emails a Tax Credit Summary PDF every January with your system cost and PTO date. It's also under Billing → Documents.
  • The credit is non-refundable but can carry forward.

Please confirm eligibility with a tax professional. See also Find your permission-to-operate date.

articles.title: I forgot my Brightline Home password
articles.summary: How to reset your password and what to do if the reset email doesn't arrive.
articles.question: How do I reset my password?
articles.answer:
On the login screen tap Forgot password, enter the email on your account, and follow the link. The link expires in 30 minutes.

Not getting the email?

  • Check spam for a message from no-reply@brightlinesolar.com.
  • If you signed up with Apple or Google, use that button instead — there is no password to reset.
  • Multiple people in the household? The account is tied to the email on the installation contract. Other household members need to be added as household members.

articles.title: Why does the app keep logging me out?
articles.summary: Session expiry rules and device limits for Brightline Home.
articles.question: I have to log in every few days. Is something wrong?
articles.answer:
Sessions last 30 days on mobile and 24 hours on the web. You'll also be logged out of all devices when:

  • You change your password
  • You enable or disable two-factor authentication
  • A new device signs in and you're already at the 5-device limit (oldest session is dropped)

If you're logged out more often than this, update the app — versions older than 4.2 have a known token-refresh bug on iOS.

articles.title: What do the alert colors in Brightline Home mean?
articles.summary: Meaning of green, amber, and red system status and which alerts need action.
articles.question: My app shows an amber dot. Do I need to do something?
articles.answer:

articles.title: Can I export my production data?
articles.summary: CSV export options and the date ranges available.
articles.question: I want my production history in a spreadsheet.
articles.answer:
Yes. Reports → Export produces a CSV with hourly, daily, or monthly granularity. Limits:

  • Hourly: up to 90 days per export
  • Daily: up to 3 years
  • Monthly: full system lifetime

Columns: timestamp, production_kwh, consumption_kwh, grid_import_kwh, grid_export_kwh, battery_soc_pct. Consumption columns are empty unless you have a consumption meter installed. Developers can pull the same data from the Partner API.

articles.title: How long does the whole installation process take?
articles.summary: Typical timeline from signed contract to permission to operate.
articles.question: I signed last week. When will my system be turned on?
articles.answer:
The national average from contract to permission to operate (PTO) is 8–12 weeks. The install itself is one or two days; everything else is paperwork and waiting on third parties.

  1. Site survey — 1 week
  2. Design & engineering — 1 week
  3. Permits — 2–6 weeks, varies by city (see permit timelines)
  4. Installation — 1–2 days
  5. Inspection — 1–2 weeks
  6. Utility PTO — 1–4 weeks

Track your stage under Account → Installation status.

articles.title: Do I need to apply for permits myself?
articles.summary: Who handles building and electrical permits for a Brightline installation.
articles.question: Do I have to go to city hall?
articles.answer:
No. Brightline files all building and electrical permits and schedules the inspection. You may be asked to:

  • Sign a permit application (electronically, in the app)
  • Provide HOA approval if your HOA requires it — we provide the standard packet
  • Be home for the inspection (most cities require an adult present)

articles.title: Set up autopay
articles.summary: Enroll a bank account or card for automatic monthly payments.
articles.body:
Before you start: have your bank routing and account number, or a card, ready. Autopay drafts on the 10th of each month.

Steps

  1. Open Brightline Home and go to Billing → Payment methods.
  2. Tap Add payment method and choose Bank account or Card.
  3. Enter the details and tap Verify. Bank accounts receive two micro-deposits within 2 business days; return to this screen to confirm the amounts.
  4. Once verified, toggle Use for autopay.
  5. Confirm the authorization text and tap Enable autopay.

To turn autopay off

Return to Payment methods, open the method, and toggle Use for autopay off. Do this at least 3 business days before the 10th to avoid that month's draft.

You can choose the 1st, 8th, 15th, or 22nd. Changes take effect the following billing cycle.

  2. Under Invoice date, select a new date.
  3. Review the one-time prorated invoice shown on screen. This covers the gap between your old and new dates.

articles.summary: Give another person view or manage access to Brightline Home.

Only the account owner (the person on the contract) can add members.

articles.title: Restart your inverter
articles.summary: Safe power-cycle procedure for the inverter when the app shows a red alert.
articles.body:
Safety: do not open any enclosure. This procedure only uses the external switches and breakers.

Steps

  1. Locate the AC disconnect (grey box next to your utility meter) and switch it OFF.
  2. Locate the DC disconnect on the inverter and switch it OFF.
  3. Wait 5 minutes. The inverter display will go dark.
  4. Switch the DC disconnect ON.
  5. Switch the AC disconnect ON.
  6. Wait up to 10 minutes for the inverter to reconnect to the grid. The display should show a production reading.

If the alert persists after 30 minutes, submit a service request.

articles.title: Reconnect the monitoring gateway to Wi-Fi
articles.summary: Restore data reporting after a router change or outage.
articles.body:
The gateway is the small white box near your inverter or electrical panel. A grey status in the app almost always means it lost Wi-Fi.

  1. In Brightline Home go to Account → System → Gateway → Reconnect.
  2. Press and hold the gateway's button for 3 seconds until the LED blinks blue.
  3. In the app, choose your home network and enter the password.
  4. Wait for the LED to turn solid green (about 1 minute).

Still grey?

  • 5 GHz-only networks are not supported; the gateway needs a 2.4 GHz network.
  • Passwords with emoji or non-Latin characters fail silently. Use a guest network if needed.

articles.title: Report low or zero production
articles.summary: Open a service request with the information the field team needs.
articles.body:
1. Go to Support → New request → Production issue.
  2. Select the date the problem started. The app attaches the production history automatically.
  3. Answer the checklist (restart attempted, visible damage, recent roof work).
  4. Add photos of the inverter display if possible.
  5. Submit.

You'll get a ticket number by email. Remote diagnostics happen within 1 business day; on-site visits are scheduled within 5.

articles.title: Clean your solar panels safely
articles.summary: When cleaning helps, when it doesn't, and how to do it without voiding the warranty.
articles.body:
Do you actually need to?

Rain handles most dust. Clean only if production is down 10%+ and you can see visible film, pollen, or bird droppings.

Method

  1. Clean early morning or evening when panels are cool.
  2. Use a garden hose from the ground. Never get on the roof.
  3. For stubborn spots, a soft brush on an extension pole with plain water.

Never use

  • Pressure washers
  • Soap, detergents, or glass cleaner
  • Hard or hot water on hot panels (thermal shock can crack glass)

Damage from any of the above is not covered by warranty.

articles.title: Get a Partner API access token
articles.summary: OAuth client credentials flow for server-to-server integrations.
articles.body:
Prerequisite: a Partner API application with a client ID and secret from the Partner Portal.

Request

POST https://api.brightlinesolar.com/oauth/token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=YOUR_ID&client_secret=YOUR_SECRET&scope=sites:read production:read

Response

{
  "access_token": "eyJ...",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "expires_in": 3600
}

Cache the token and refresh it before expiry. Tokens are not revoked on rotation of the secret for 10 minutes, giving you a rollover window.

Next: Partner API overview.

articles.title: Export production history in bulk
articles.summary: Use the asynchronous export endpoint for large date ranges.
articles.body:
1. Create a job: 
    POST /v2/exports
{ "site_ids": ["..."], "from": "2025-01-01", "to": "2025-12-31", "granularity": "hourly" }

  3. Download download_url (a signed URL valid for 1 hour). Files are gzipped CSV.

Jobs are limited to 500 sites and 3 years each. Export jobs do not count against the per-request rate limit.

articles.title: What is net metering and how does it show on my bill?
articles.summary: How exported energy is credited by your utility and where to find it.
articles.question: The app says I exported 340 kWh last month. Where's my credit?
articles.answer:
Net metering is a utility program, not a Brightline program. Your utility credits exported kWh against imported kWh on its bill, usually on a line labelled Net Energy Metering or NEM credit. Brightline Home displays the export figure from your meter so you can verify it.

  • Credits typically roll over month to month.
  • Many utilities settle annually ("true-up") and pay out or zero any remaining balance.
  • Some utilities have moved to net billing, which credits exports at a lower rate than imports.

If the utility figure differs from the app by more than 5%, contact support with both bills attached.

articles.title: Will my battery keep the lights on during an outage?
articles.summary: What a backup battery powers, for how long, and how to check reserve.
articles.question: We lose power a few times a year. What does the battery actually run?
articles.answer:
Depends on what was wired to the backup panel at install. Check Account → System → Backup circuits. Typical whole-home setups exclude the HVAC compressor and electric range.

Runtime

A 13.5 kWh battery runs essential circuits (fridge, lights, Wi-Fi, outlets) for roughly 18–24 hours without sun, and indefinitely with sun if you avoid high-draw appliances.

Reserve setting

Account → System → Battery → Backup reserve sets how much to hold back for outages. Default is 20%; raise it before a storm.

articles.title: Set up a webhook for alert events
articles.summary: Receive alert.opened and alert.closed events instead of polling.
articles.body:
1. Register an endpoint: 
    POST /v2/webhooks
{ "url": "https://example.com/hooks/brightline", "events": ["alert.opened", "alert.closed", "site.pto"] }
  2. Store the returned signing_secret.
  3. Verify each delivery by computing HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body with the secret and comparing to the X-Brightline-Signature header.
  4. Respond with 2xx within 5 seconds. Failed deliveries retry with exponential backoff for 24 hours.

Payload example:

{
  "event": "alert.opened",
  "site_id": "st_48a1",
  "severity": "red",
  "occurred_at": "2026-06-12T14:03:00Z"
}

articles.title: Can I get one combined invoice for all my properties?
articles.summary: Explains how to enable consolidated billing across multiple properties under a single Brightline multi-property account.
articles.question: I own several homes that all have Brightline Solar systems. Right now I'm getting separate invoices for each address. Is there a way to combine them into one monthly bill?
articles.answer:
Consolidated Billing for Multi-Property Accounts

Yes — if you have two or more active Brightline systems registered under the same owner email address, you can enroll in Consolidated Billing at no extra charge. Once enrolled, a single invoice is issued on the same date each month and covers all properties.

How to Enable Consolidated Billing

  1. Open Brightline Home and tap Account → Properties.
  2. Confirm all properties appear under your profile. If a property is missing, tap Add Property and enter the system serial number (format: BLS-XXXXXXXX) and the service zip code.
  3. Tap Billing Settings → Consolidated Invoice, then toggle On.
  4. Choose a Primary Property — this address will appear as the billing address on the combined invoice.
  5. Tap Save. Changes take effect on your next invoice cycle.

What the Consolidated Invoice Shows

ColumnDetails
PropertyFull service address
System IDBLS-XXXXXXXX
Production (kWh)Month-to-date generation
Amount DuePer-property charge
Combined TotalSum of all properties

Each property's line item is still individually downloadable. See how to download a PDF invoice for steps. For questions about your invoice date, visit when are invoices issued.

Note: Consolidated Billing is not yet available for accounts mixing loan-financed and lease-financed systems. Full support is planned for Q3 2025.

articles.title: Can I use different payment methods for each property on my account?
articles.summary: Explains how to assign separate autopay payment methods to individual properties within a multi-property Brightline account.
articles.question: I manage billing for several rental properties under one Brightline account. Can I link a different bank account or card to each property so the charges go to the right place automatically?
articles.answer:
Per-Property Payment Methods

Yes. Brightline Home supports per-property autopay, letting you assign a distinct payment method to each address on your account. This is useful for landlords, property managers, and investors who track expenses separately per property.

How to Set a Payment Method Per Property

  1. In Brightline Home, go to Account → Properties and select the property you want to configure.
  2. Tap Billing → Payment Method.
  3. Choose an existing saved method or tap Add New to enter a bank account (ACH) or credit/debit card.
  4. Toggle Autopay to On for that property.
  5. Repeat for each additional property.

Important Rules

  • Each property can have one active autopay method at a time.
  • If you have Consolidated Billing enabled, per-property payment methods are not supported — one payment method covers the combined total. Disable Consolidated Billing first (Billing Settings → Consolidated Invoice → Off) to restore per-property control.
  • Credit card payments incur a $2.75 convenience fee per transaction. ACH payments are free. See our recent credit card fee update for details.
  • Autopay drafts occur on your individual property billing date, which may differ per property unless you've aligned them. To change a date, see how to change your billing date.

If a payment fails for one property, only that property's autopay is paused — other properties are unaffected. You'll receive an in-app alert and an email within 24 hours of any failed draft.

articles.title: How do I add or remove a property from my multi-property account?
articles.summary: Learn how to link a new Brightline Solar installation to your existing account or unlink a property you no longer own.
articles.question: I own multiple homes with Brightline Solar panels. How do I add a new property to my account, and what happens to billing if I sell one of my homes?
articles.answer:
Adding a Property

You can link an additional Brightline Solar installation to your account directly in the Brightline Home app:

  1. Open the app and tap Account in the bottom navigation bar.
  2. Select My Properties, then tap + Add Property.
  3. Enter the Property ID found on your installation completion letter or on the original welcome email for that address.
  4. Confirm ownership by entering the last four digits of the bank account or card on file for that property.

Once verified, the new property appears in your dashboard within 24 hours. Each property retains its own billing cycle unless you opt into a consolidated invoice — see Multi-Property Consolidated Invoice for details.

Removing or Transferring a Property

If you sell a home, you must formally unlink the property to avoid continued billing responsibility. Contact Brightline Support at least 14 days before closing and provide:

  • The property address and Property ID
  • Closing date
  • New owner's name and email (if transferring the solar agreement)

Billing for that property stops on the closing date you provide. Any prorated credit or outstanding balance is applied to your next invoice on your remaining properties. Note: failing to notify us before closing may result in a $35 late-transfer processing fee. For questions about payment options across properties, visit What Payment Methods Are Accepted.

articles.title: Why do my properties show different charges on the same billing date?
articles.summary: Explains why invoice amounts can vary across properties in a multi-property account and how to identify the source of a discrepancy.
articles.question: I have three properties under one Brightline account. This month two of them have noticeably higher charges than usual, but the third looks normal. What could be causing the difference?
articles.answer:
Why Charges Differ Between Properties

Each property in a multi-property account is billed independently based on its own system size, local utility rate, net-metering agreement, and loan or lease terms. Common reasons two properties might spike while a third stays flat include:

  • Seasonal production variance: Shading, roof orientation, or local weather can affect each site differently.
  • Rate plan changes: Utility rate adjustments roll out by ZIP code and may not affect all your properties simultaneously.
  • Battery dispatch settings: If one property's battery is set to Self-Supply mode while another uses Backup Only, grid import and therefore charges can diverge significantly.
  • Loan vs. lease structure: Properties on different financing products have different monthly base fees that can amplify apparent differences.

How to Investigate

  1. In the Brightline Home app, tap Account → My Properties and select the affected property.
  2. Tap Invoices and open the current month's invoice. Look for line items flagged with a yellow ! icon — these indicate an estimated read or a utility true-up adjustment.
  3. Compare the Production Summary panel for each property side by side using the Compare Properties toggle (available in app version 4.3 and later).

If a charge still looks incorrect after reviewing, use the Dispute This Charge button at the bottom of the invoice detail screen. Disputes are reviewed within 5 business days. For broader guidance on unexpected charges, see Why Is My Bill Higher Than Expected or learn about invoice timing at When Are Invoices Issued.

articles.title: Why did my autopay fail and how do I fix it?
articles.summary: Learn the common reasons autopay payments fail and the exact steps to resolve each one before a late fee is applied.
articles.question: My autopay didn't go through and I received a failed payment notification. Why did this happen and what do I need to do to fix it?
articles.answer:
Why Autopay Payments Fail

When an autopay attempt is unsuccessful, Brightline Home sends you an in-app alert and an email within 30 minutes of the failed transaction. The notification includes a short error code to help identify the cause. Common codes and their meanings are listed below.

Error CodeCause
PAY-401Insufficient funds or credit limit reached
PAY-402Card expired or bank account closed
PAY-403Billing address mismatch
PAY-404Payment method removed from account
PAY-405Bank blocked the transaction (contact your bank)

How to Resolve a Failed Payment

  1. Open Brightline Home and tap Account → Billing → Payment Methods.
  2. Verify that your saved card or bank account details are current and the billing address matches your bank's records.
  3. If the method is outdated, tap Edit or Add New Method and save your changes.
  4. Return to Billing → Outstanding Balance and tap Pay Now to manually submit the missed payment.

Retry Window and Late Fees

Brightline automatically retries a failed autopay once, 48 hours after the original due date. If the retry also fails, a $9.95 late fee is added to your next invoice. To avoid this fee, resolve the issue and pay manually before the retry date shown in your alert.

For a full list of accepted payment types, see What payment methods are accepted? If you need to update your autopay enrollment, visit Set up autopay.

articles.title: My autopay is enabled but no payment was taken on my due date — what's wrong?
articles.summary: Understand why an active autopay enrollment might not charge on your due date and how to confirm your payment will process correctly.
articles.question: I have autopay turned on in my account, but my due date passed and I wasn't charged anything. My invoice still shows as unpaid. Is something wrong with my account?
articles.answer:
Common Reasons Autopay Doesn't Trigger

Even when autopay is enabled, several conditions can prevent a charge from processing on your due date:

  • Enrollment completed too close to the due date: If you enrolled in autopay fewer than 3 business days before your bill was due, the current invoice is excluded from autopay. You must pay it manually, and autopay will apply starting with your next invoice.
  • Invoice not yet finalized: Autopay only fires after your invoice status changes to Finalized. If there is a usage calculation delay, finalization — and therefore the charge — may shift by 1–2 days. See When are invoices issued? for the typical schedule.
  • Two-factor authentication locked the account: If your account was locked due to a security event, autopay is paused until you log in and confirm your identity. Visit Enable two-factor authentication to review your security settings.
  • Billing date was recently changed: A billing date change shifts the due date of your current cycle, which can create a gap where no charge appears on the original date.

How to Confirm Your Autopay Status

  1. In Brightline Home, go to Account → Billing → Autopay Settings.
  2. Confirm the toggle shows Active and that the correct payment method is listed as the default.
  3. Check the Next Scheduled Payment field — if it shows a future date, autopay is working correctly.

Paying a Skipped Invoice

If your invoice is overdue, go to Billing → Outstanding Balance and tap Pay Now to submit a one-time manual payment and prevent a late fee.

articles.title: Why did autopay charge me a different amount than my invoice shows?
articles.summary: Explains why your autopay charge may not match your invoice total and how to resolve common discrepancies.
articles.question: My autopay payment went through, but the amount that was charged to my bank account or card is different from what I see on my invoice in the Brightline Home app. Why does this happen and how do I fix it?
articles.answer:
Why the Charged Amount May Differ

A mismatch between your autopay charge and your invoice total is usually caused by one of the following:

  • Credit card convenience fee: If your payment method is a credit card, a 2.1% processing fee is added at the time of charge. This fee does not appear on the base invoice. See our credit card fee update article for details.
  • Pending invoice adjustment: If your utility reported a net-metering true-up after your invoice was generated, your balance may have been revised before autopay ran. The app will show the revised figure under Billing > Invoice History, but email confirmations sometimes reflect the earlier amount.
  • Partial credit applied: A referral credit, warranty adjustment, or prior overpayment credit may have reduced the amount actually collected.
  • Timing of rate changes: If your financing rate adjusted on the same billing cycle, the first charge under the new rate may differ from the previous month.

How to Verify the Correct Amount

  1. Open Brightline Home and go to Account > Billing > Invoice History.
  2. Tap the relevant invoice and select Download PDF to see the final itemized total.
  3. Compare the PDF total with your bank or card statement.

Still Don't Recognize the Charge?

If the discrepancy is not explained by the items above, contact Brightline Solar Support at 1-800-555-0174 or use in-app chat. Have your invoice number (format: BL-XXXXXXXX) ready. Disputes must be submitted within 60 days of the charge date. You can also review how to download your invoice PDF for a full breakdown.

articles.title: How do I update the payment method on my autopay before the next charge?
articles.summary: Step-by-step guide to changing or replacing the bank account or card linked to your Brightline autopay enrollment before your next due date.
articles.question: My credit card expired and I have a new card number, or I want to switch autopay from my card to my bank account. How do I update my payment method so the next scheduled autopay doesn't fail?
articles.answer:
Deadline to Update

Changes to your autopay payment method must be saved at least 3 business days before your due date to take effect for the upcoming charge. Updates made after that window will apply starting the following billing cycle, and the current cycle may require a manual one-time payment to avoid a $15 late-payment fee.

How to Update in Brightline Home

  1. Open the app and tap Account (bottom-right icon).
  2. Select Billing & Payments > Autopay Settings.
  3. Tap Change Payment Method.
  4. Choose Add New Bank Account (ACH, no fee) or Add New Card (Visa, Mastercard, or Discover; 2.1% fee applies).
  5. Enter your new payment details and tap Verify & Save.
  6. You will receive a confirmation email to your address on file within 15 minutes. If you do not receive it, check your spam folder or update your contact details at Update Contact Information.

Removing an Old Payment Method

After saving a new method, your previous card or account will appear as Inactive. To delete it entirely, tap the method and select Remove. You cannot remove a payment method while it is designated as your active autopay source.

Accepted Payment Methods

For a full list of accepted payment types and any associated fees, see What payment methods are accepted?

Need Help?

If you see error code PAY-4031 when saving a new method, your bank may be blocking the verification micro-deposit. Contact your bank to whitelist Brightline Solar (ACH company ID: 1254087632), then retry.

articles.title: Sign In to Brightline Home with Apple
articles.summary: Link your Apple ID to your Brightline Home account so you can log in with Face ID, Touch ID, or your Apple password instead of a separate Brightline password.
articles.body:
Before you begin: You must have an existing Brightline Home account registered with an email address that matches your Apple ID, or be prepared to confirm a one-time merge prompt. Your device must run iOS 15 or later. If you have two-factor authentication enabled on your Brightline account, you will not be prompted for a second factor after linking—Apple's own authentication satisfies that requirement.

  1. Open Brightline Home and tap Log In on the welcome screen.
  2. Tap Continue with Apple beneath the email and password fields.
  3. Authenticate with Face ID, Touch ID, or your Apple ID password when prompted by your device.
  4. If your Apple ID email matches your Brightline account email exactly, you are signed in immediately. Skip to step 6.
  5. If the emails differ, Brightline displays a Merge Account prompt. Enter your existing Brightline password to confirm the merge, then tap Link Accounts. This is a one-time step.
  6. You land on the Home dashboard. A confirmation banner reads Apple Sign-In enabled for this account.
  7. On future visits, tap Continue with Apple to sign in without entering any Brightline credentials.

Troubleshooting

Error BL-AUTH-4031 – Email mismatch, merge failed: This appears when the Brightline password you entered in step 5 is incorrect. Tap Forgot password? and follow the steps in Reset your Brightline Home password before retrying the merge.

Stuck on the Apple consent screen: Force-close Brightline Home, open Settings > Apple ID > Password & Security > Apps Using Apple ID, and remove any existing Brightline entry. Then retry from step 1.

Sign-in succeeds but you see someone else's account: Another household member may have previously linked their Apple ID on this device. Sign out via Profile > Sign Out, then complete steps 1–4 with your own Apple ID. See also Add a household member to your account to understand how shared-device access works.

articles.title: Sign In to Brightline Home with Google
articles.summary: Connect your Google account to Brightline Home so you can authenticate with a single tap using your existing Google credentials.
articles.body:
Before you begin: You need a Brightline Home account already created (either by you during onboarding or provisioned by Brightline after installation). The Google account you use must be active and accessible on your device. Brightline Home version 4.2 or later is required on Android; version 4.1 or later on iOS. Check Profile > App Version if you are unsure.

  1. Open Brightline Home and tap Log In.
  2. Tap Continue with Google below the standard login fields.
  3. Select the Google account you want to use from the account picker. If your account is not listed, tap Add account and sign into Google first.
  4. Review the Brightline permissions screen and tap Allow. Brightline requests read access to your email address only; no Google Drive or Calendar access is requested.
  5. If your Google email matches your Brightline account email, you are signed in and land on the Home dashboard. A green banner confirms Google Sign-In linked successfully. Skip to step 7.
  6. If the emails differ, Brightline shows a Link Existing Account dialog. Enter your Brightline password and tap Confirm Link. After confirmation, the Google account is permanently associated and the password prompt will not appear again.
  7. On future logins, tap Continue with Google and select your account—no password entry is needed.

Troubleshooting

Error BL-AUTH-4050 – Google token invalid: Your Google session may have expired. Open your device's Google app, sign out and back in, then retry steps 1–4 in Brightline Home.

Error BL-AUTH-4055 – Account already linked to a different Google ID: Only one Google account can be linked at a time. To switch Google accounts, go to Profile > Security > Linked Accounts > Google > Unlink, then repeat this procedure with the new account. Note that unlinking does not disable your ability to log in with your email and password.

Unexpected logout after linking: Sessions established before linking are invalidated as a security measure. This is expected behavior; simply sign in again with Google. For more on session expiration policies, see Why was I logged out of Brightline Home?

Cannot find the Continue with Google button: Your app may be outdated. Update Brightline Home from the App Store or Google Play, then retry. Release details are available in Brightline Home 4.3 release notes.

articles.title: How do I manage my notification preferences in the Brightline Home app?
articles.summary: Step-by-step guide to customizing which alerts and updates you receive from Brightline Home, and how to choose your preferred delivery channels.
articles.question: How do I control which notifications I get from Brightline Home? I'm getting too many emails and want to turn some off.
articles.answer:
Accessing Notification Preferences

To manage your notifications, open the Brightline Home app, tap the Profile icon in the bottom-right corner, then go to Settings > Notification Preferences. On the web portal, navigate to My Account > Profile > Notifications.

Available Notification Categories

You can enable or disable notifications independently for each of the following categories:

  • Production Alerts – Low output warnings, daily production summaries, and record generation days.
  • Billing & Payments – Invoice ready, payment confirmed, autopay reminders, and failed payment notices.
  • System Health – Inverter offline, gateway disconnection, and firmware update alerts.
  • Outage & Battery – Grid outage detected and battery charge level warnings.
  • Account & Security – Login from a new device, password changes, and two-factor prompts.

Delivery Channels

For each category you can choose one or more delivery channels:

  • Push notification (mobile app only)
  • Email
  • SMS – requires a verified mobile number under Profile > Contact Information

Changes save automatically. Allow up to 5 minutes for new preferences to take effect across all channels.

Important: Can't Turn Off All Notifications

Account & Security notifications cannot be fully disabled; at least one channel must remain active to protect your account.

For related help, see What do the alert colors mean? and Update contact information.

articles.title: Why aren't my notification preference changes saving in the app?
articles.summary: Troubleshooting steps for when your notification settings revert or fail to save in the Brightline Home app.
articles.question: I keep turning off certain notifications but they come back on the next time I open the app. Why won't my notification preferences save?
articles.answer:
Common Causes

If your notification preferences appear to reset, one of the following issues is usually responsible:

  • App version out of date – Preference syncing requires Brightline Home version 4.2.0 or later. Go to your device's app store and update if needed.
  • Session timeout during save – If your session expired while you were on the Notifications screen, changes may not have been written to your account. Look for error code PREF-401 in the in-app notification banner.
  • Multiple devices overwriting each other – If you are signed in on two or more devices and save different settings on each within a short window, the last save wins. Sign out of unused devices under Profile > Active Sessions.
  • OS-level permissions overriding in-app settings – On iOS and Android, the operating system has its own notification toggle for Brightline Home. If OS permissions are set to Deny, push notifications will not arrive even if enabled in the app.

Steps to Fix

  1. Update the app to the latest version.
  2. Sign out and sign back in, then re-apply your preferences.
  3. Check OS notification permissions: iOS – Settings > Brightline Home > Notifications; Android – Settings > Apps > Brightline Home > Notifications.
  4. If error code PREF-503 appears, wait 15 minutes and try again — this indicates a temporary server sync issue.

If the problem persists after these steps, contact Brightline Solar Support with your account email and the error code displayed. See also Why was I logged out? and Enable two-factor authentication.

articles.title: Set Up Alert Notifications in Brightline Home
articles.summary: Configure which system alerts you receive and how they are delivered through the Brightline Home app.
articles.body:
Before you begin: You must be signed in to the Brightline Home app (version 4.0 or later) on iOS or Android. Alert delivery options include push notifications, email, and SMS. SMS alerts require a verified mobile number on your account. See manage-notification-preferences if you only need to adjust existing preferences rather than set them up for the first time.

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and tap the Menu icon (three lines, top-left corner).
  2. Select Settings, then tap Notifications & Alerts.
  3. Under Alert Categories, you will see four groups: Production, Equipment, Battery, and Billing. Tap each category to expand it.
  4. Toggle on any alert type you want to receive. Common selections include Inverter Offline (Equipment), Low Production Warning (Production), and Battery Charge Below 20% (Battery).
  5. For each enabled alert, tap Delivery Method and choose one or more of: Push Notification, Email, or SMS. SMS is available only if a verified mobile number is saved to your account.
  6. Under Quiet Hours, optionally set a time window (e.g., 10 PM–7 AM) during which non-critical alerts will be held and delivered as a morning digest instead of in real time.
  7. Tap Save Preferences at the bottom of the screen. You will see a confirmation banner: "Alert preferences updated."
  8. To confirm delivery is working, tap Send Test Alert. A test push notification, email, or SMS (matching your chosen methods) will arrive within two minutes.

Troubleshooting

Test alert never arrived: Check that your device's OS-level notification permissions are enabled for the Brightline Home app under your phone's Settings > Apps > Brightline Home > Notifications. For email, inspect your spam or junk folder; add alerts@brightlinesolar.com to your contacts to prevent filtering.

SMS option is greyed out: Your mobile number has not been verified. Go to Settings > Account > Contact Information and complete verification, or see update-contact-information for step-by-step guidance.

"Save Preferences" button does nothing: This is often caused by a temporary session issue. Force-close and reopen the app, then repeat the steps. If the problem persists after two attempts, see notification-preferences-not-saving.

Alert colors are unfamiliar: Each alert is color-coded by severity. See what-do-the-alert-colors-mean for a full reference.

articles.title: Dismiss or Snooze an Active Alert in Brightline Home
articles.summary: Clear a resolved alert from your dashboard or temporarily snooze a recurring alert so it does not reappear for a set period.
articles.body:
Before you begin: You must be signed in to the Brightline Home app. Only the account owner and any household members granted Manager or higher access can dismiss alerts; members with Viewer access can read alerts but cannot dismiss or snooze them. To understand what a colored alert badge means before acting on it, review what-do-the-alert-colors-mean first.

  1. Open the Brightline Home app. Active alerts appear as a numbered badge on the Alerts bell icon in the bottom navigation bar.
  2. Tap the Alerts icon to open the Alert Center. Each alert card shows the alert title, severity color, timestamp, and a brief description.
  3. Tap the alert card you want to act on to open its detail view.
  4. To dismiss the alert (mark it as resolved and remove it from the active list): tap Dismiss Alert at the bottom of the detail view. A dialog will ask you to confirm: "Mark this alert as resolved? It will move to your Alert History." Tap Confirm. The alert disappears from the active list within five seconds and is stored in Alert History for 90 days.
  5. To snooze the alert (keep it on record but suppress repeat notifications temporarily): tap Snooze, then choose a duration — 1 hour, 4 hours, Until tomorrow morning (7 AM), or Custom. Custom allows you to pick any duration up to 7 days. Tap Apply Snooze. A snooze icon (clock badge) appears on the alert card.
  6. To review past dismissed alerts, go to Alerts > Alert History. Tap any historical alert to see its full detail, including which account user dismissed it and when.

Troubleshooting

"Dismiss Alert" button is missing: Your account role may be Viewer. Ask the account owner to upgrade your access level under Settings > Household Members, or see add-household-member.

Alert reappears immediately after dismissal: If the underlying system condition (e.g., inverter offline, low production) is still active, the Brightline Home system will automatically reopen the alert within 15 minutes of detection. Dismissing an alert does not resolve the equipment issue. For an inverter offline alert, follow the steps in restart-inverter; for low production, see report-low-production.

Snooze duration expired but issue is still unresolved: The alert will re-enter your active list at the end of the snooze window. This is by design to ensure ongoing issues are not overlooked. Apply another snooze or escalate by contacting Brightline Solar support via the in-app chat.

Alert History is empty after 90 days: Dismissed alerts are automatically purged after 90 days. If you need a record of historical alerts for warranty or insurance purposes, contact Brightline Solar support to request an alert log export before the 90-day window closes.

articles.title: What should I do to prepare for my solar installation day?
articles.summary: A checklist of steps homeowners should complete before the installation crew arrives to ensure a smooth, on-schedule visit.
articles.question: My installation is coming up and I want to make sure everything goes smoothly. What do I need to do to get ready before the crew shows up?
articles.answer:
Before Installation Day

A little preparation goes a long way. Complete the steps below at least 48 hours before your scheduled start time to avoid delays or rescheduling fees.

Access & Clearances

  • Unlock all access points — the crew needs entry to your roof, attic hatch (if applicable), main electrical panel, and garage if your battery or inverter is being installed there.
  • Clear a 3-foot work zone around your main breaker panel and any interior wall where conduit will run.
  • Secure pets indoors or off-site for the full day; the crew may need to move freely through side gates and yards.
  • Trim overhanging branches if any hang within 18 inches of the planned panel layout — your installer cannot work under them safely.

On the Day

  1. An adult (18+) who is a named account holder or authorized contact must be present for the full installation window, typically 7 a.m. – 5 p.m.
  2. Your crew lead will call or text 30 minutes before arrival using the mobile number on your account. Make sure it's current at update-contact-information.
  3. Expect one planned utility power outage of roughly 15–45 minutes while the crew ties into your panel.

Permits

Brightline pulls all required permits on your behalf. If you'd like to confirm permit status before the visit, see do-i-need-a-permit.

Questions? Contact your Installation Coordinator via the Brightline Home app under My Project → Messages.

articles.title: Does someone have to be home the entire time during my solar installation?
articles.summary: Explains the homeowner presence requirements on installation day, including who qualifies and what happens if no authorized adult is available.
articles.question: I work during the day and I'm not sure I can be home the whole time. Does someone really need to be there all day for the solar installation, or can the crew work without me?
articles.answer:
Presence Requirement

Yes — Brightline Solar requires a responsible adult (18 or older) to be present for the entire installation window. This is a firm policy, not just a recommendation, for three reasons:

  • The crew lead must perform a walk-through inspection with you at the start of the visit to confirm the agreed-upon panel layout and equipment placement.
  • You must sign the Installation Completion Certificate at the end of the visit before the crew can close out the job.
  • If unexpected structural or electrical conditions arise, the crew lead needs immediate authorization to proceed or reschedule specific work items.

Who Counts as an Authorized Adult?

The person present must be either the primary account holder or someone you've added as an authorized household member. You can add someone in the Brightline Home app under Settings → Household → Add Member — see add-household-member for step-by-step instructions.

If No One Can Be There

Contact your Installation Coordinator at least 72 hours in advance to reschedule at no charge. Rescheduling with less than 24 hours' notice incurs a $95 short-notice fee. Same-day no-shows are charged $195 and may delay your project by 2–4 weeks depending on crew availability in your region. Learn how to reschedule without fees at reschedule-installation.

Typical Installation Window

Most residential installations run 6–10 hours. If your system includes battery storage, allow up to 12 hours. You'll receive a narrower 2-hour arrival window via text the evening before.

articles.title: What actually happens on installation day, step by step?
articles.summary: A walkthrough of the typical sequence of events during a Brightline Solar residential installation, from crew arrival to end-of-day handoff.
articles.question: My installation is coming up and I want to know what to expect. What will the crew do throughout the day, and how long will each part take?
articles.answer:
Installation Day Overview

A standard Brightline Solar installation typically runs 6–10 hours, depending on system size and roof complexity. Here is what to expect at each stage:

1. Crew Arrival (8:00–9:00 AM local time)

Your lead installer will introduce themselves, review the site plan with you, and walk the property. Please make sure your driveway and side-gate access are clear before they arrive.

2. Roof Work (2–5 hours)

The crew mounts racking hardware, lays conduit, and secures panels. Power to your home will remain on during this phase.

3. Electrical Work (1–2 hours)

Installers connect the inverter and any battery storage to your main panel. Expect one or two brief outages of 10–20 minutes each during this phase. Do not run sensitive equipment such as home servers or medical devices during this window.

4. System Commissioning (30–60 minutes)

The lead installer powers on the system, verifies communication with the Brightline Gateway, and confirms your panels appear in the Brightline Home app. You will receive an in-app notification once monitoring is live.

5. Homeowner Walkthrough

Before leaving, your installer reviews the breaker locations, explains the alert light colors on your inverter, and answers questions. They will also confirm your Permission to Operate (PTO) application has been submitted — note that PTO from your utility may take additional days or weeks. See how to find your Permission to Operate date and how long installation takes for more detail.

articles.title: Can my pets be outside during installation, and what other safety rules apply on installation day?
articles.summary: Guidelines for keeping pets, children, and household members safe while the Brightline Solar crew works on your property.
articles.question: I have two dogs and a toddler. Are there any safety rules I need to follow on installation day? Can my pets be in the yard while the crew is working?
articles.answer:
Safety Guidelines for Installation Day

Your family's safety — and the crew's — is our top priority. Please follow the guidelines below on the day of your installation.

Pets

  • Keep all pets indoors or in a secured area away from the work zone for the entire installation day. Tools, screws, and cable offcuts on the ground pose a hazard, and open doors during electrical work create escape opportunities.
  • If a crew member needs to access an area where a pet is present, work may pause until the animal is safely moved, which can add time to your appointment.

Children

  • Children under 18 should remain at least 10 feet away from active work areas, including the roof perimeter, the electrical panel, and any staging zones in the driveway.
  • A responsible adult (18+) must be on the premises throughout the appointment. For details on who qualifies, see who needs to be home on installation day.

General Household Prep

  • Clear a 3-foot path to your main electrical panel and any sub-panels.
  • Remove vehicles from the driveway so crew trucks and equipment trailers can park close to the home.
  • Expect brief power interruptions; power down desktop computers and unplug sensitive electronics beforehand.

If circumstances change and you need to adjust your appointment, visit how to reschedule your installation for steps to modify your booking without a fee up to 72 hours in advance.

articles.title: Crew Arrival Windows Shrinking from 4 Hours to 2 Hours Starting July 14
articles.summary: Brightline Solar is reducing installation crew arrival windows from a four-hour block to a two-hour block, giving customers more flexibility on installation day.
articles.abstract: Beginning July 14, 2025, all newly scheduled and rescheduled residential installations will receive a two-hour crew arrival window instead of the previous four-hour window, so you spend less time waiting and can plan the rest of your day with confidence.
articles.body:
Effective date: July 14, 2025

We heard your feedback: waiting half a day for a crew to arrive is inconvenient. Starting July 14, every installation appointment will carry a two-hour arrival window confirmed 48 hours in advance by push notification and email.

How windows are assigned

  • Morning window: 7:00 AM – 9:00 AM crew arrival
  • Midday window: 10:00 AM – 12:00 PM crew arrival
  • Afternoon window: 1:00 PM – 3:00 PM crew arrival

You can view your assigned window in Brightline Home → Appointments → Upcoming at any time. A real-time crew-tracking map will appear in the app on the morning of your installation once the crew departs their staging location.

Appointments booked before July 14 retain their original four-hour windows unless you reschedule. See how to reschedule your installation if you would like to move to the new two-hour system sooner.

Questions? Contact scheduling support at 1-800-555-0174, Monday–Friday 7 AM – 6 PM local time.

articles.title: New: Real-Time Crew Arrival Window Adjustments Sent via App Alerts on Installation Day
articles.summary: Brightline Solar now pushes live crew arrival window updates directly through the Brightline Home app so customers always have the latest estimated time, even when schedules shift.
articles.abstract: As of June 2, 2025, Brightline Home will automatically send in-app and SMS notifications if your crew's arrival window changes on the day of installation due to traffic, a prior job running long, or weather delays, replacing the previous practice of customers calling in to check on status.
articles.body:

Same-day delays happen. Until now, customers had to call our scheduling line to find out whether a crew was running late. That changes today with real-time arrival window updates delivered directly through Brightline Home.

What you will receive

Crew departs stagingPush + in-app mapMorning of install

Crew 15 min awayPush + SMSAutomatically

Notifications are on by default for all accounts. To customize which channels you receive alerts on, visit manage notification preferences in your account settings.

If your window shifts by more than 90 minutes and the new time no longer works for you, a no-fee same-day reschedule option will appear inside the notification. Standard reschedule fees of $75 do not apply when Brightline initiates the change.

articles.title: Utility Interconnection Reviews Running 4–6 Weeks Longer This Summer
articles.summary: Several regional utilities have expanded their technical review queues, pushing interconnection approval timelines out by four to six weeks starting June 2025.
articles.abstract: Beginning in June 2025, Brightline Solar has observed significant delays in utility interconnection approvals across multiple service territories, primarily driven by grid modernization audits and increased residential solar application volumes. Customers whose systems are fully installed and inspected may experience a longer wait before receiving Permission to Operate (PTO) and should not attempt to activate their systems until written PTO confirmation is received from their utility.
articles.body:
Effective June 1, 2025, interconnection review periods have extended in the following regions:

  • Pacific Southwest territories: 10–14 weeks (previously 6–8 weeks)
  • Southeast coastal territories: 8–12 weeks (previously 5–7 weeks)
  • Midwest territories: 6–10 weeks (previously 4–6 weeks)

These delays are caused by utility-side staffing constraints and mandatory grid-stability reviews introduced under new state regulations in Q2 2025. Brightline Solar is submitting all interconnection applications within 3 business days of passing municipal inspection and will notify you by push notification and email at each status change.

MilestoneWho ActsTypical Duration
Application SubmittedBrightline SolarWithin 3 business days post-inspection
Utility Technical ReviewYour UtilitySee regional list above
PTO Letter IssuedYour Utility1–3 business days after approval

To check your current interconnection status and PTO date, visit How to Find Your Permission to Operate Date. For general permit timeline context by region, see our updated Permit Timelines by Region guide.

articles.title: Utilities Now Require Additional Documentation for Interconnection Applications
articles.summary: Starting August 15, 2025, several utilities are requiring a new Homeowner Authorization Form as part of the interconnection application package, and Brightline Solar will contact affected customers to collect signatures.
articles.abstract: A growing number of utility companies in Brightline Solar's service territories have updated their interconnection application requirements to include a signed Homeowner Authorization Form (HAF-2025), which verifies that the property owner consents to grid-tied operation and acknowledges net metering terms. Customers with pending interconnection applications submitted after August 15, 2025 may receive an in-app document request; failure to sign within the deadline can pause the application and delay Permission to Operate.
articles.body:
Effective August 15, 2025, the following utilities have added the HAF-2025 to their required interconnection packages:

  • Sunvale Municipal Power (Pacific Southwest)
  • Coastal Energy Cooperative (Southeast)
  • Lakeshore Electric Authority (Midwest)
  • Ridgeline Power District (Mountain West)

If your system's interconnection application falls under one of these utilities, you will receive an in-app alert and email within 2 business days of your application submission asking you to complete the HAF-2025 digitally inside the Brightline Home app under Account > Permits & Documents > Pending Signatures.

Important deadlines:

  • Customers have 10 calendar days to sign after receiving the request.
  • Unsigned forms will cause a 30-day application hold imposed by the utility.
  • No additional fee is charged by Brightline Solar for resubmission, but utility resubmission fees of up to $75 may apply.

To understand how interconnection fits into the broader installation journey, see How Long Does Installation Take?. Questions about net metering terms referenced in the HAF-2025 can be found in What Is Net Metering?

articles.title: Request Historic District Permit Approval for Your Solar Installation
articles.summary: Walk through the steps to submit required historic district review documents so Brightline Solar can obtain local architectural board approval before your installation begins.
articles.body:
Before you begin: Confirm that your property is located within a designated historic district by checking your county assessor's website or your Brightline Home app under My Home > Property Details > Jurisdiction Flags. Historic district review adds an average of 6–10 weeks to the standard permit timeline. You will need digital copies (PDF or JPEG, max 20 MB each) of your property's deed, current exterior photographs from all four elevations, and any prior Certificate of Appropriateness (COA) documents issued by your local Historic Preservation Commission (HPC). Your installation timeline will not be confirmed until HPC approval is received. See how-long-does-installation-take for general timeline expectations.

  1. Open the Brightline Home app and tap My Home > Documents > Upload Permit Documents.
  2. Select Historic District Review Package from the document type dropdown.
  3. Upload all required files: deed, four-elevation photos, and any existing COA documents. Tap Save & Submit.
  4. Within 2 business days, your assigned Brightline Permit Specialist will email you a draft Panel Placement Diagram and a completed HPC application form for your review. Reply with any corrections within 5 business days.
  5. Brightline will submit the finalized HPC application on your behalf. You will receive an in-app notification (status: HPC Submission Confirmed) once the application is filed.
  6. Monitor review status in the app under My Home > Permit Tracker. Status updates to HPC Approved or HPC Revision Requested as decisions are made.
  7. If a revision is requested, your Permit Specialist will contact you within 3 business days with required changes. Repeat steps 3–6 as needed.
  8. Once HPC approval is granted, Brightline files the standard building permit automatically. You will receive a final Permit Issued notification before your installation date is confirmed.

Troubleshooting

Upload fails with error HD-412: Your file exceeds the 20 MB size limit or is not in PDF or JPEG format. Compress the file and retry.

No email from your Permit Specialist after 3 business days: Check your spam folder for messages from permits@brightlinesolar.com, then tap Help > Contact Permit Team in the app to open a support ticket.

HPC Revision Requested status is stuck: If the status has not updated within 5 business days after you resubmitted documents, contact your Permit Specialist directly using the callback number shown in the Permit Tracker panel.

Note: A $149 Historic District Processing Fee applies to all HPC submissions and will appear on your next invoice. For regional permit timing details, see permit-timelines-by-region.

articles.title: Appeal a Historic District Permit Denial for Your Solar Project
articles.summary: Follow these steps to formally appeal an Historic Preservation Commission denial so Brightline Solar can pursue an alternative panel placement or design that meets local guidelines.
articles.body:
Before you begin: You must have received an official HPC denial letter, which Brightline uploads to your account under My Home > Documents > Permit Correspondence within 2 business days of receipt. Appeals must be initiated within 30 calendar days of the denial date printed on the letter; requests outside this window require a full new HPC application. Note that filing an appeal does not guarantee approval, and installation cannot proceed until a valid permit is issued. For general permit requirements, see do-i-need-a-permit.

  1. In the Brightline Home app, navigate to My Home > Permit Tracker and tap the HPC Denied status badge to open the denial summary.
  2. Review the listed denial reasons. Common reasons include panel visibility from a public right-of-way, reflective surface concerns, or non-conforming mounting hardware.
  3. Tap Start Appeal. Select one of three response options: Revised Placement Design, Alternative Low-Profile Panel Submission, or Formal Written Appeal with Supporting Evidence.
  4. Your Permit Specialist will schedule a 30-minute video consultation (within 5 business days) to discuss your chosen option. Accept the calendar invite sent to your account email.
  5. After the consultation, Brightline prepares revised drawings or a formal appeal brief. You will receive a PDF preview in the app for approval. Review and tap Approve & Submit Appeal within 7 business days.
  6. Brightline submits the appeal to the HPC. Most jurisdictions schedule an appeal hearing within 4–8 weeks. Your Permit Tracker will update to Appeal Hearing Scheduled with the hearing date displayed.
  7. Attend the HPC hearing if your jurisdiction requires homeowner presence. Your Permit Specialist will advise you at least 14 days in advance if attendance is mandatory.
  8. After the hearing, Brightline updates your Permit Tracker to Appeal Approved or Appeal Denied – Final. If approved, your installation date is scheduled within 10 business days.

Troubleshooting

Start Appeal button is grayed out: The 30-day appeal window may have expired, or your denial letter has not yet been uploaded. Contact your Permit Specialist via Help > Contact Permit Team to confirm document receipt.

Video consultation link is not working: Use the backup dial-in number included in your calendar invite. If you did not receive an invite, check spam for calendar@brightlinesolar.com and then open a support ticket in the app.

Appeal Hearing Scheduled status shows no date: Some jurisdictions do not release hearing dates until 10 days before the meeting. If the field remains blank beyond 30 days, tap Request Status Update in the Permit Tracker to prompt your specialist.

Final denial received: If the appeal is unsuccessful, Brightline will propose a ground-mount or carport-mount alternative where zoning allows. A revised site assessment ($199 fee) will be required to evaluate feasibility. For expected timelines at each stage, see permit-timelines-by-region.

articles.title: Understand the Monitoring Subscription Line on Your Invoice
articles.summary: Learn what the monthly monitoring subscription charge on your Brightline invoice covers and how to verify it is correct.
articles.body:
Before you begin: You will need access to your Brightline Home account and at least one issued invoice. The monitoring subscription fee is $9.99/month for standard plans and $14.99/month for plans that include battery management. This line appears on every invoice as Brightline Monitoring & App Services.

  1. Open the Brightline Home app or sign in at my.brightlinesolar.com.
  2. Tap Account in the bottom navigation bar, then select Billing & Invoices.
  3. Tap the invoice you want to review. If you need a PDF copy, see Download an Invoice PDF.
  4. Scroll to the Service Charges section. Locate the line labeled Brightline Monitoring & App Services.
  5. Confirm the amount matches your plan tier. Your plan tier is shown under Account > Plan Details.
  6. If the amount is higher than expected, check whether a prorated charge applies. Prorated amounts appear when your billing date changed mid-cycle or when a battery module was added to your system during the billing period.
  7. If the charge still looks incorrect, tap Dispute This Charge at the bottom of the invoice detail screen and follow the on-screen prompts. A support case is created automatically and you will receive a confirmation email within one business day.

Troubleshooting

I see two monitoring lines on the same invoice. This can occur after a plan upgrade processes mid-cycle. The first line covers the old rate for days 1–15 and the second covers the new rate for days 16–end. Both lines together should equal a single full month at the blended rate. If the combined total does not match, use Dispute This Charge as described in step 7.

The Brightline Monitoring & App Services line is missing entirely. Invoices generated within 24 hours of account creation may omit this line due to a known delay in plan provisioning. Wait one billing cycle; if the line is still absent, contact support so your plan can be relinked. You will not be charged retroactively for a missed line caused by a provisioning error.

For questions about autopay and how charges are collected, see Set Up Autopay.

articles.title: Request a Waiver or Adjustment for the Monitoring Subscription Line
articles.summary: Submit a formal adjustment request if you believe the monitoring subscription charge on your invoice was applied in error or qualifies for a waiver under Brightline's service-credit policy.
articles.body:
Before you begin: Only the primary account owner can submit an adjustment request. You must have the invoice number ready and the request must be submitted within 60 days of the invoice date; requests outside this window are not eligible for adjustment. Waivers are granted in limited circumstances, including: gateway offline for more than 15 consecutive days through no fault of the customer (error code GW-OFFLINE-15), duplicate billing caused by a system migration, or a documented service outage affecting the Brightline Home app for more than 72 hours in the billing period.

  1. Sign in to Brightline Home and navigate to Account > Billing & Invoices.
  2. Select the invoice containing the monitoring subscription line you want to dispute.
  3. Tap Dispute This Charge, then choose Request Waiver or Adjustment from the reason menu.
  4. Select the applicable reason from the dropdown: Gateway Offline, Duplicate Charge, App Service Outage, or Other.
  5. In the Details field, describe the issue in at least two sentences. If you have supporting screenshots or gateway logs, tap Attach Files (JPEG, PNG, or PDF, max 10 MB each).
  6. Tap Submit Request. You will see confirmation code formatted as ADJ-XXXXXXX. Save this code for your records.
  7. Brightline's billing team will review your request within 5–7 business days. You will receive an email at your account address with the decision and, if approved, the credit amount and the invoice or statement cycle it will appear on.
  8. If your request is denied and you believe the decision is incorrect, reply to the decision email with subject line RE: ADJ-XXXXXXX Appeal to escalate to a senior billing specialist.

Troubleshooting

The "Dispute This Charge" button is greyed out. This indicates the invoice is older than 60 days or has already been paid and closed with no open dispute window. Contact support directly via Account > Help > Chat with Us and provide your invoice number; an agent can manually open a case for exceptional circumstances.

I submitted a request but never received a confirmation code. The confirmation screen may time out if your session expires during submission. Check Account > Billing & Invoices > Dispute History to see whether the request was recorded. If it does not appear there, resubmit using the same steps above. Duplicate submissions are automatically merged by the billing system.

My credit was approved but has not appeared after two billing cycles. Credits are applied to the next closed invoice after approval. If two full cycles have passed, contact support and reference your ADJ-XXXXXXX code. To review how credits interact with automatic payments, see Autopay Deducted the Wrong Amount and Download an Invoice PDF.

articles.title: What do all the line items on my Brightline Solar invoice mean?
articles.summary: A plain-language breakdown of every charge and credit that may appear on your monthly Brightline Solar invoice.
articles.question: I just received my invoice and I'm confused by some of the line items—things like 'Solar Service Fee,' 'Net Production Credit,' and 'Carry-Forward Balance.' What does each one actually mean?
articles.answer:
Invoice Line Items Explained

Your monthly Brightline Solar invoice is organized into three sections: Charges, Credits, and Summary. Here is what each line item means:

Charges

Line ItemWhat It Is
Solar Service FeeYour fixed monthly charge for system access, monitoring, and support. This amount is set in your financing agreement and does not change month to month.
Monitoring SubscriptionA $4.99/month fee for advanced Brightline Home app features including real-time alerts and historical exports. See Understanding the Monitoring Subscription Line for details.
Late Payment FeeA $15.00 fee applied when a balance remains unpaid 10 days after the due date.
Credit Card Convenience FeeA 2.1% fee added when paying by credit card. See our fee change notice for background.

Credits

  • Net Production Credit: A bill reduction calculated from the kilowatt-hours your system exported to the grid under your net-metering agreement.
  • Carry-Forward Credit: Unused credit from a previous billing period rolled into the current invoice. Credits accumulate for up to 12 months before expiring.
  • Referral Credit: A one-time $150 credit applied after a referred customer reaches Permission to Operate.

Summary

The Amount Due line reflects all charges minus all credits. If the result is negative, the surplus appears as a carry-forward credit on your next invoice—you will never receive a cash refund for credit balances under $50.00.

articles.title: Why is my invoice total higher than I expected this month?
articles.summary: Common reasons your Brightline Solar invoice may be larger than usual, and steps to investigate or dispute unexpected charges.
articles.question: My invoice this month is noticeably higher than normal. I haven't changed anything—why would my bill go up, and what can I do about it?
articles.answer:
Why Your Invoice May Be Higher Than Usual

Several factors can cause a one-time or recurring increase in your invoice total. Work through the checklist below to identify the cause.

1. Reduced Net Production Credit

If your system produced less electricity than usual—due to seasonal shading, soiling, or an inverter issue—your Net Production Credit will be smaller, leaving a higher balance. Check your production history in the Brightline Home app under Home > Production > Monthly View. If output looks abnormally low, see Report Low Production to open a service ticket.

2. Carry-Forward Balance from a Missed Payment

A prior unpaid balance plus a $15.00 late fee may have rolled into this invoice. Review the Previous Balance line at the top of your invoice PDF. To avoid future late fees, consider enrolling in autopay at Set Up Autopay.

3. New or Changed Fees

Occasionally Brightline Solar adjusts ancillary fees with 30 days' written notice. Check your email for a notice with subject line Important Update to Your Brightline Solar Account, or review the fee history section in the app under Account > Billing > Fee History.

4. Prorated Charges After a Billing Date Change

If you recently moved your billing date, a prorated invoice covering a partial period may appear larger than a standard monthly bill. This is a one-time occurrence.

Still Unclear?

Download your full invoice PDF for an itemized view, then contact Brightline Support via Account > Help > Chat with your invoice number (format: BLS-YYYYMM-XXXXX) ready. Our billing team can issue a credit within 5 business days if an error is confirmed.

articles.title: How do I read my Brightline Solar invoice?
articles.summary: A section-by-section walkthrough of every part of your monthly Brightline Solar invoice.
articles.question: I just received my invoice and I'm not sure what all the sections and numbers mean. Can you walk me through how to read it?
articles.answer:
Invoice Header

The top of your invoice shows your Account Number (format: BLS-XXXXXXXX), your service address, and the Statement Date—the date the invoice was generated. Your Due Date is always 21 days after the Statement Date unless you have a custom billing date (see Change your billing date).

Summary Box

Just below the header you'll find a shaded summary box with three figures:

  • Previous Balance: Any unpaid amount carried from your last statement.
  • Payments Received: Credits applied since your last statement, including AutoPay transactions.
  • Amount Due Now: The total you owe by the Due Date.

Line Items Section

This section breaks your charges into individual rows. Common line items include:

Line ItemWhat It Covers
Solar Lease / Loan PaymentYour monthly financing installment
Monitoring Subscription$9.99/mo for Brightline Home app access and production alerts
Battery Management FeeApplies only to accounts with a Brightline PowerVault battery
Late Fee$15.00 assessed if prior balance was not paid within 5 days of due date

Production Summary

At the bottom of the invoice you'll see a 30-day production snapshot (kWh generated) pulled directly from your system's monitoring data. If these numbers look off, visit Report low production.

Need the PDF?

You can download a print-ready copy of any invoice from the Brightline Home app under Billing → Statements → Download PDF. For step-by-step instructions, see Download invoice PDF.

articles.title: Why is my invoice total different from last month?
articles.summary: Common reasons your Brightline invoice amount changed and how to investigate each one.
articles.question: My invoice this month is higher (or lower) than usual and I wasn't expecting it to change. What could have caused this?
articles.answer:
Most Common Reasons for a Change

Your monthly total can shift for several reasons. Work through the list below to identify the cause on your specific invoice.

  1. Prorated charge or credit: If your billing date recently changed, or you added a battery mid-cycle, you'll see a one-time prorated line item that won't appear next month.
  2. Monitoring Subscription adjustment: The $9.99/mo Monitoring Subscription fee may have been waived, reinstated, or adjusted. See Understand the monitoring subscription line on your invoice for a full explanation.
  3. Late fee applied: A $15.00 late fee is added automatically if your previous balance was not settled within 5 days of its due date. This appears as "Late Payment Fee – [date]" in the Line Items section.
  4. Financing rate step-up: Some promotional loan agreements include scheduled rate increases at 12, 24, or 60 months. Check page 2 of your original loan agreement for a rate schedule, or open Brightline Home → Billing → Financing Details to view your current rate tier.
  5. Credit card convenience fee: If you recently switched from bank-transfer (ACH) payments to a credit card, a 2.9% convenience fee now applies to each transaction. See Credit card fee change for details.
  6. Outstanding balance carried forward: A missed or partial AutoPay payment from a prior month may have rolled into this statement. Visit AutoPay failed – what to do if you suspect a payment didn't process correctly.

Still Can't Identify the Difference?

Open your last two invoices side by side using Billing → Statements in the Brightline Home app and compare each line item individually. If a charge still appears unexplained, tap Get Help on the invoice screen to start a billing inquiry and our team will respond within 2 business days.

articles.title: SMS Verification Codes Delayed Due to Carrier Routing Issue — July 2025

articles.title: Why You May Not Be Receiving SMS Login Codes — Tips and Known Fixes
articles.summary: Brightline Home users who never receive SMS two-factor codes can use this guide to diagnose common causes and switch to a more reliable verification method.
articles.abstract: SMS one-time codes are a key part of Brightline Home's two-factor authentication flow, but several factors — including carrier filtering, VoIP numbers, and international roaming — can prevent codes from arriving. This article explains the most common causes and provides step-by-step fixes, including how to switch to an authenticator app for a more dependable login experience.
articles.body:
If you tap Send Code on the Brightline Home login screen and nothing arrives, one or more of the following issues is likely the cause:

CauseSymptomsFix
